body.statement: The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) is nonempty in both mixed and two-heavy regimes. Set \(d_1(x)=x\) and \(d_0(x)=1-x\). A mixed neighborhood is generated by \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(\pi_1(x)=x^{3/2}/2\), \(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\), and \(Y(a)=a+X+\zeta\) with centered logistic \(\zeta\): here \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}=\{1\}\), \(\gamma_1=5/3\), \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}=\{0\}\), and \(\gamma_0=\infty\) under the bounded-support convention. A two-heavy neighborhood is generated by \(\pi_1(x)=x^{\alpha_1}/\{x^{\alpha_1}+(1-x)^{\alpha_0}\}\) and \(\pi_0=1-\pi_1\), with compact \(\alpha_a>1\). Both neighborhoods obey common Hall, endpoint-score, and density moduli; the mixed center has nonzero treated endpoint drift at \(\tau=1/2\).
body.justification: The explicit neighborhoods reconcile binary propensity coherence with either one or two weak-overlap endpoints.
body.gap: The oracle anchor imposes lawwise tail behavior but does not construct a uniform smooth class for a growing propensity likelihood.
body.consumer: These neighborhoods provide legal mixed-branch and two-heavy designs for the expansion and simulations.
body.proof_tex:
For the mixed family, let \(X\) be uniform, let \(\zeta\) be centered logistic and independent of \(X\), draw \(A\mid X=x\) with success probability \(x^{3/2}/2\), and put \(Y(a)=a+X+\zeta\).  Consistency holds by the definition of \(Y\), and independence of \(\zeta\) from the treatment draw gives unconfoundedness.  Positivity holds away from the two null endpoints.  For \(0<t<1/2\),
\[
 F_1^\pi(t)=P\{X\le(2t)^{2/3}\}=2^{2/3}t^{2/3}.
\]
Thus \(\gamma_1=5/3\), \(c_1=2^{2/3}\), and the Hall remainder is zero.  Since \(\pi_0\ge1/2\), \(\gamma_0=\infty\) and \(E_P(1/\pi_0)\le2\).

Take \(g_1=-\log2\) and \(g_0(x)=\log(1-x^{3/2}/2)\).  Then the former paired links hold, and \(\text{lem:paired-links-imply-joint-logit}\) gives
\[
 \eta(x)=\frac32\log x-\log(2-x^{3/2}),
 \qquad (\pi_1,\pi_0)=(\Lambda(\eta),\Lambda(-\eta)).
\]
Both \(g_a\) lie in a fixed \(C^{3/2}\) ball.  Opposite overlap holds near zero because \(\pi_1\le1/2\).

Writing \(\lambda(z)=e^{-z}(1+e^{-z})^{-2}\),
\[
 f_{a\mid X}(y\mid x)=\lambda(y-a-x),
 \qquad
 m_{a,\tau}(x)=\tau-\Lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}.
\]
Boundedness of \(\lambda\) and \(\lambda'\) gives the common conditional-density and score moduli.  Also
\[
 f_a(\tau)=\int_0^1\lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}\,dx>0,
\]
and finiteness of \(\mathcal A\times\mathcal T\) gives a positive common minimum.  Given \(\pi_1(X)=t\), \(X=(2t)^{2/3}\); hence the Lipschitz property of \(\Lambda\) gives
\[
 |\kappa_{1,\tau}(t)-\kappa_{1,\tau}(0)|
 \le \|\lambda\|_\infty(2t)^{2/3}.
\]
Taking \(G_1\) as the law of \(1+\zeta\) verifies the endpoint mark condition.  Symmetry of \(X+\zeta\) about \(1/2\) yields \(q_1(1/2)=3/2\), and
\[
 m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{1,1/2}=\frac12-\Lambda(1/2)\ne0.
\]

For the two-heavy family, retain the outcome construction and take the displayed odds.  Then
\[
 \eta(x)=\alpha_1\log x-\alpha_0\log(1-x),
\]
so the joint boundary link holds with \(g_0=g_1=0\).  At zero, \(\pi_1(x)=x^{\alpha_1}\{1+O(x^{\min(1,\alpha_1)})\}\); at one, \(\pi_0(x)=(1-x)^{\alpha_0}\{1+O((1-x)^{\min(1,\alpha_0)})\}\).  Monotone inversion under the uniform design gives
\[
 F_a^\pi(t)=c_at^{1/\alpha_a}\{1+O(t^{\rho_a})\},
 \qquad \gamma_a=1+\alpha_a^{-1}\in(1,2).
\]
Compactness supplies common constants and moduli.  The endpoints are disjoint, so opposite overlap holds on fixed endpoint neighborhoods.  The preceding logistic outcome calculations verify the remaining outcome and mark assumptions.  Thus both families belong to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\).
